name: DigitalOcean
summary: Developer cloud for running apps, APIs and databases: virtual servers (Droplets), a managed app platform, managed databases, Kubernetes, object storage and on-demand GPUs, billed per second.
best_for: developers and small teams who want to run an app, API or database on plain cloud infrastructure with published per-second prices, from a free static site on App Platform or a $4 Droplet up to managed Kubernetes and on-demand GPUs
skip_if: you want someone else to look after the server and the software on it — a managed host such as Cloudways, which DigitalOcean owns and lists from $11 a month on the same pricing page, does that for more money — or you do not want to administer a server at all
honest_knock: The $4 Droplet is real, but it is the smallest machine — 512 MiB of memory — and it is only the server. Backups cost 20% (weekly) or 30% (daily) of the Droplet price on top, a managed database starts at $15 a month and a load balancer at $12, so a small production app is several line items rather than one: a 2 GiB Droplet at $12 with daily backups ($3.60) and the smallest managed database ($15) comes to $30.60 a month before any bandwidth overage. Billing is per second and in arrears, which is fair, but the bill arrives after the month you used — set a billing alert on day one.

pricing.plans_source: hand-curated from the vendor's pricing page
pricing.notes: (read 3 October 2026 on digitalocean.com/pricing and its Droplets, App Platform, GPU Droplets and Managed Databases pages) DigitalOcean is pay-as-you-go cloud infrastructure: you rent the pieces and pay per piece. Basic Droplets (virtual servers) run from $4 a month for 512 MiB, 1 vCPU, 10 GiB of SSD and 500 GiB of outbound transfer, through $6 (1 GiB), $12 (2 GiB), $18, $24 and $48 up to $96 a month for 16 GiB and 8 vCPUs. Since 1 January 2026 Droplets are billed per second, with a minimum of 60 seconds or $0.01. Backups are extra: 20% of the Droplet price for weekly or 30% for daily, and outbound transfer beyond the allowance is $0.01 per GiB. App Platform has a free tier for three static-site apps (1 GiB of transfer each, further static apps $3 each); apps with a server start at $5 a month for a fixed container with 1 vCPU and 512 MiB, limited to one instance, then $10, $12, $25 and $50, with a $7 development database, a $25 dedicated egress IP and $0.02 per GiB beyond the bandwidth allowance. Managed databases start at $15 a month, managed Kubernetes at $12, load balancers at $12 and Spaces object storage at $5. GPU Droplets run on demand from $0.76 per GPU-hour (RTX 4000 Ada) through $1.57 (L40S) to $4.41 (H100) and $4.47 (H200); a 12-month reservation brings the H100 to $3.26, and the GPU page says new pricing took effect on 1 August 2026. DigitalOcean also owns Cloudways and lists its managed hosting from $11 a month on the same pricing page. Billing is monthly in arrears: the card is charged on the first day of the month for the previous month's usage, or earlier if usage passes a threshold.

compare_with.name: Cloudways
compare_with.why: DigitalOcean owns Cloudways and sells both: a Droplet is the raw server you run yourself, while Cloudways puts a managed WordPress and PHP stack with platform support on a cloud server for more per month. Choose on how much server work you want to do.
